blocks.text: With Mia Kidis, Daia, Anya Beyersdorf
Courtesy of Preliminary Materials Films Pty Ltd

Mia is happily aimless, working odd jobs and hanging with friends. But when she’s scouted to become a model, new people and strange conundrums enter the frame. Showcasing an array of new talent, both in front of and behind the camera, Lee’s inventive exploration of the absurdity of 20-something life, unfolding against the backdrop of late-stage capitalism, is a welcome and unexpected breath of fresh cinematic air.
Contains scenes of graphic violence or injury.
Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .
For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.
If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.
More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

blocks.text: A young man embarks on a surreal quest to find his long-lost father in a remarkable feature debut that spans 20 years of recent Chinese history.
This bold debut, set over the course of one sweltering day, follows a 17-year-old working as a ‘tee-girl’ at a golf club.
A talking fox, voiced by Olivia Colman, persuades a hunter to transform his cheating wife into an ideal spouse, in this gleefully outrageous, shape-shifting comedy.
